scope: 25 exact historical keys outside other assignments; exact operators and endpoint meanings/stances compared with source-grounded parent components.

rows.review_disposition: Retire the broad movement-structure edge with heterogeneity explicit in 9EDD/677352 and the relevant actor parents. Ideological division is one component; courts, popular rebels, agents and foreign interests must not collapse into that binary.

56435 must retain the propertied and heterogeneous Vendémiaire coalition and uncertainty over royalism. Preserve the government’s attempt to recover substantial citizens’ support rather than a blanket royalist label.
5B270 can internalize Belgian resistance limiting deportation enforcement. Preserve the concentration of refusers, official hesitation and liability-versus-actual-transport distinction.

0848 can internalize state control within the Concordat settlement. Keep religious freedom, majority status, property settlement and stronger papal spiritual authority distinct from salaried institutional dependence.

2E013 can internalize Fructidor disrupting Lille through removal of moderates and hardening terms. Preserve the actual political mechanism and British maritime bargaining position, not just chronological succession.

B973’s local instance route is not equivalent to making the entire southern conflict an effect of the later oath/schism. Preserve earlier sectarian conflict and the inventory trigger separately; religious reforms and repression intensified organized opposition with lay agency, not a single uniform origin.

29CD must retain parliamentary opposition as a qualified possibility for unpurged Jacobins. Retirement of an abstract target must not turn Doyle’s counterfactual into either proven democratic innocence or inevitable constitutional overthrow.

CB77 can internalize refusal to widen the franchise as continuity of the propertied foundation. Preserve the apparent tension with temporary Jacobin support rather than treating the later policy as a new constitutional design.
381386 must retain categorical deprivation of noble citizenship and weak enforcement on 334. The radical wording is not evidence that every noble was actually expelled or lost practical citizenship.

04E/C479 can retain Pillnitz within great-power policy, with its conditions and royalist misreading. A repeated part_of edge can retire without portraying a unified unconditional restoration commitment.

7593 must retain militarization and the collapse of the princely force after allied retreat, while 4F5D preserves Condé’s exception. Louis XVIII’s later claim is not the destination for the whole military process; avoid autonomous-army strength claims.

29CD/F4D can internalize official candidate lists, rival assemblies and verification powers as pre-election engineering. Distinguish these preparations from the later Floréal annulment and from the earlier Fructidor coup.

Quiberon and the Irish expedition are distinct failed interventions linked only broadly by Hoche and cross-Channel strategy. Retire the generic related edge, preserving each mechanism and chronology; 211–212 alone do not evidence the 1796 Irish expedition.

E268 can internalize the contrast between limited Catholic relief and the United Irishmen’s later underground/French-supported course. Preserve the transition and distinct populations, not an assumption that relief satisfied all reform demands.

4E189 must retain the multi-causal subsistence crisis making radical criticism persuasive. Retire the unbound revival target only with the political effect explicit and without claiming every sufferer became a Jacobin or communist.

5193/F6ED must preserve assignat collapse prompting the attempted replacement, with the rejected bank alternative and mandates’ separate failure. The old causes operator is a policy-response sequence, not an inevitable successful solution.

3F2B can internalize Jourdan’s country-in-danger proposal as the last major initiative of the 1799 resurgence and its rejection as a limit. Preserve fear of exceptional government despite real military danger.

21A/0D88/0364 must retain generals’ support for the triumvirs because concessions threatened military gains and prestige. Retire the broad supports edge only with that named political motive and alignment explicit.

Retire the weak relation between 1795 ratification and later electoral disengagement. Preserve low turnout and the separate manipulated Two Thirds mandate in CB77/667E, and later limited protest in 9DE8 without interpreting abstention as approval of coups.

43E040 and 612D must retain Granville’s earlier failed linkage and Quiberon’s later distinct organization. A precursor edge can retire if their chronology and changed actors are explicit; 309–310 alone do not establish every later Quiberon detail.

Preserve the design/practice contrast between Year III separation and Fructidor’s army-backed coercion in CB77/48B. The old page 319 supports design, while the later event needs 330–331; do not claim same-page equivalence.

733FB can internalize persistent Catholic practice limiting Theophilanthropy’s reach. Preserve Sundays, Grégoire’s constitutional Church, official favour and weak adoption rather than a successful replacement narrative.

4E189 can internalize distress contributing to social resentment and radicalization. Keep environmental, monetary, military and market causes and distinguish mobilization from universal acceptance of Babeuf.

CB77 must retain bicameralism as a concrete check with distinct initiating and reviewing chambers. The abstract checks-and-balances node is unnecessary once the mechanism and intended purpose are explicit.

7593/677352 must retain noble status conflict as a contributor to factional division, balanced with sincere sacrifice and loyalism. A broad contribution edge can retire if that mechanism remains, not if all divisions become abstract ideology.
